Visit note | 2025-02-02 02:30 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Nabila Karim, 58, female. Mrs. Karim presents complaining of a highly uncomfortable rash with spreading edges, consisting of a ring-shaped itchy red rash. She reports that the itch is worse in humid weather. She is a ride-share driver and notes the symptoms started after playing football on wet fields in Bashundhara. She has a history of Hypothyroidism. She denies any joint pain, fever, or similar lesions elsewhere on her body. On examination, her vitals are BP 130/82 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 86 kg. Skin examination reveals the affected area about 8 cm across on her lower leg with active, scaling borders. Assessment: Tinea corporis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep the skin dry, do not share towels, and wash clothes in hot water. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-02-02 02:30 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Dalia Talukder, 54, female. Mrs. Talukder presents with redness and irritation in both eyes, noting that both eyes are affected and symptoms are worse in certain seasons. She works as a call centre agent and reports that her condition became significantly worse after cleaning a dusty storeroom in Sirajganj. She has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies any eye pain, photophobia, or discharge. On examination, visual acuity 6/18 in the right eye, BP 126/75 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 59 kg. Bilateral conjunctival injection with mild chemosis is noted. Assessment: Allergic conjunctivitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid rubbing the eyes, use cool compresses, and wear sunglasses outdoors. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-02-02 02:30 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Rokeya Ahmed, 24, female. Ms. Ahmed presents with sudden attacks of a racing heart and severe breathlessness during attacks, noting that she has had normal heart tests previously. She works as a tailor and reports that these attacks began after a traffic accident in Rampura. She has a history of Hypothyroidism. She denies any chest pain, syncope, or history of substance abuse. On examination, her vitals are BP 114/80 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 88 kg. She has experienced about 6 panic attacks in the last month. Mental status examination shows mild anxiety but is otherwise unremarkable. Assessment: Panic disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to practise slow breathing during attacks, reduce caffeine, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-02-02 03:00 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Rozina Molla, 22, female. Ms. Molla presents with a gnawing pain in the upper belly, particularly noting pain that wakes them at night. She is a software developer and states that this discomfort started after weeks of taking painkillers for back pain in Kushtia. She has a comorbidity of Hypothyroidism. She denies any vomiting, melena, hematemesis, or unexplained weight loss. On examination, her vitals are BP 127/82 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 67 kg, and her pain score 5/10. Mild epigastric tenderness is noted on abdominal palpation. Assessment: Peptic ulcer disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen, stop smoking, and eat regular meals. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a stool H. pylori test.

Visit note | 2025-02-02 03:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Sumaiya Molla, 75, female. Mrs. Molla presents with sudden dizziness when looking up, which is accompanied by a spinning sensation and nausea with the spinning. She is a madrasa teacher and reports that the symptoms began after bumping the head on a rickshaw hood in Sirajganj. She has a history of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies any hearing loss, tinnitus, or focal weakness. On examination, her vitals are BP 129/71 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 54 kg. The Dix-Hallpike test positive on the left side, which successfully reproduced her transient nystagmus. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-02-02 03:00 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Arafat Majumder, 54, male. Mr. Majumder complains of a blocked ear after a cold and moderate ear pain. He is an accountant and notes that his ear discomfort started after swimming in a pond in Gulshan. He has a comorbidity of Hypothyroidism. He denies any discharge from the ear, dizziness, or hearing loss in the unaffected ear. On examination, otoscopy reveals an erythematous, bulging tympanic membrane with loss of light reflex. His temperature 101.2°F, BP 120/81 mmHg, pulse 103 bpm, weight 57 kg. Assessment: Acute otitis media. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep the ear dry and do not insert cotton buds. Follow-up in 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-02-02 03:00 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Nargis Ahmed, 19, female. Ms. Ahmed presents with concerns regarding persistent acne and extra hair on the face. She is a homemaker and noticed these changes after a friend in Farmgate suggested testing. There are no known comorbidities. She denies any voice deepening, abnormal weight gain, or pelvic pain. On examination, her BMI 25.7, BP 113/85 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 59 kg. Mild facial acne and moderate hirsutism are observed. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-02-02 03:30 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Saiful Howlader, 60, male. Mr. Howlader presents with itchy eyes, sneezing fits, and symptoms worse with dust. He works as a restaurant cook and reports that his symptoms have been worse since keeping a cat at home in Jatrabari. There are no comorbidities. He denies any fever, sore throat, or shortness of breath. On examination, his nasal mucosa is pale and boggy. Vitals are BP 120/79 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 67 kg. The patient reports experiencing about 8 sneezing fits a day. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-02-02 03:30 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Rehana Dewan, 66, female. Mrs. Dewan presents with a red eye, sticky yellow discharge, and eyelids stuck together in the morning. She works as a shopkeeper and notes that the symptoms began after swimming at a public pool in Rajshahi. There are no comorbidities. She denies any severe pain, photophobia, or vision changes in the other eye. On examination, conjunctival injection with purulent discharge is observed. Visual acuity 6/9 in the left eye, BP 132/79 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 77 kg. Assessment: Bacterial conjunctivitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to wash hands often, do not share towels, and stay away from work for two days. Follow-up in 1 week if not better.

Visit note | 2025-02-02 03:30 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Tasnim Sikder, 19, female. Ms. Sikder presents with persistent acne and irregular periods. Visit note | 2025-02-02 04:00 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Babul Bepari, 53, male. He is a bus driver and notes that his symptoms flare on long commutes through traffic in Rangpur. There are no comorbidities. He denies any unexplained weight loss, blood in his stool, or night-time bowel movements. On examination, his abdomen is soft and mildly distended. Vitals are BP 118/71 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 85 kg, pain score 3/10. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-02-02 04:00 PM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Tuhin Hossain, 24, male. He denies any blood in his stool, fever, or weight loss. On examination, his abdomen is soft but diffusely tender. Vitals are BP 111/70 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 70 kg, pain score 4/10. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-02-02 04:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Rashed Chowdhury, 44, male. Mr. Chowdhury presents with a band-like pressure around the head and significant stress. He works as a journalist and reports that these headaches began after a stressful house move to Old Dhaka. He has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies any nausea, vomiting, photophobia, or visual aura. On examination, there is mild pericranial muscle tenderness. Vitals show BP 117/75 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 78 kg, pain score 4/10. Assessment: Tension-type headache. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to take screen breaks every hour, do neck stretches, and sleep seven hours. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-02-03 10:00 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Tanvir Munshi, 22, male. Mr. Munshi presents with spots on the back, pimples and blackheads on the face, and marks left after pimples. He is a sales representative and reports that his skin flared after using a heavy face cream bought in Kushtia. He has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies any systemic symptoms, joint pain, or fever. On examination, facial skin shows multiple open and closed comedones with about 14 inflamed spots on the face. Vitals are BP 121/74 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 81 kg. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and do not squeeze spots. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-02-03 10:00 AM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Aminul Molla, 43, male. Mr. Molla presents with swelling of the eyelid and a painful red lump at the edge of the eyelid. He works as a police constable and reports that this began after a dusty motorbike ride in Noakhali. He has a comorbidity of Essential hypertension. He denies any vision changes, double vision, or eye discharge. On examination, there is a localized, tender lump about 5 mm on the left upper eyelid. Vitals are BP 148/86 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, weight 84 kg. Assessment: Hordeolum. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to use a warm compress four times a day, do not squeeze the lump, and avoid eye makeup. Follow-up in 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-02-03 10:30 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Tuhin Shikder, 43, male. Visit note | 2025-02-03 11:00 AM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Aminul Ahmed, 45, male. Mr. Ahmed presents with a sudden high fever, severe aching in the bones and muscles, and a faint rash on the arms. He is a schoolteacher and reports his symptoms started during the monsoon after mosquitoes bred in water tanks near Shyamoli. He has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies any active bleeding from his gums, nose, or black stools. On examination, his temperature 101.7°F, BP 125/71 mmHg, pulse 103 bpm, weight 47 kg. Laboratory results show a platelet count 110000 per microlitre. Assessment: Dengue fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, repeat the platelet count in 48 hours, and go to hospital at once for bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.

Visit note | 2025-02-03 11:30 AM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Abul Molla, 29, male. Mr. Molla presents with a twisted ankle, pain when walking, and swelling around the ankle. He works as a construction worker and reports that he twisted it while stepping off a bus in Dhanmondi. There are no comorbidities. He denies any numbness, tingling, or inability to bear weight immediately after the injury. On examination, there is localized swelling and tenderness over the lateral ligament complex of the ankle. Vitals are BP 111/77 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 82 kg, pain score 8/10. Assessment: Ankle sprain. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to rest, ice, compression, and elevation for 48 hours, and use a crepe bandage. Follow-up in 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-02-03 12:00 PM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Ruma Sarkar, 25, female. Assessment: Community-acquired pneumonia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to rest and drink plenty of fluids, and return at once if breathing becomes difficult. Follow-up in 3 days for review and a chest X-ray in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-02-04 02:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Nirmal Sen, 77, male. Mr. Sen presents with burning in both feet and a tingling like pins and needles. He is a farmer and noticed these symptoms after long hours standing at a factory in Tejgaon. There are no comorbidities. He denies any muscle weakness, gait instability, or hand involvement. On examination, neurological testing reveals reduced sensation at 4 of 10 monofilament test sites. Vitals are BP 125/80 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 87 kg. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to check the feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-02-04 02:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Hasina Gazi, 23, female. Ms. Gazi mentions she has been feeling weak with loose watery stools and bouts of vomiting. She reports these symptoms started after drinking tap water on a trip to Shyamoli. She works as a graphic designer and lives in a shared mess. She has no chronic health conditions and denies any recent travel abroad or blood in her motions. On examination: pulse 108 bpm, BP 125/75 mmHg, weight 54 kg. Her abdomen is soft with mild generalized tenderness but no guarding or peritonism. Assessment: Acute gastroenteritis. Plan: a prescription was issued for rehydration and symptom relief. She was advised to drink small sips of fluid often, eat bland foods like rice, bananas, and toast, and wash her hands carefully before eating. Follow-up in 2 days if the stools do not settle.

Visit note | 2025-02-04 03:00 PM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Nayeem Sikder, 49, male. Mr. Sikder explains he suffers from long hours looking at a screen, a constant band-like pressure around his head, and stiffness in the neck muscles. He notes the trouble began after a stressful house move to Shyamoli. He works as a restaurant cook and spends long shifts on his feet in a hot kitchen. He has no comorbid illnesses and denies visual disturbances, weakness, or fever. On examination: pain score 6/10, BP 136/74 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 63 kg. Cranial nerves are intact, and power and reflexes are normal in all limbs. Assessment: Tension-type headache. Plan: a prescription was issued to help manage muscle tension and pain. He was advised to take screen breaks every hour, do gentle neck stretches, and aim for seven hours of quality sleep at night. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-02-04 04:30 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Mehnaz Mondal, 71, female. Mrs. Mondal describes trouble falling asleep most nights, waking up tired in the morning, and persistent worry about her lack of sleep. She mentions these sleeping difficulties began after starting rotating shifts at a factory in Cox's Bazar. She works as a shopkeeper and finds the irregular hours exhausting. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a sleep diary.

Visit note | 2025-02-05 09:00 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Asif Faruque, 67, male. Mr. Faruque complains of breathlessness on effort along with chest tightness when walking fast or climbing. He states the discomfort was first felt while rushing to catch a train in Kamrangirchar. On examination: BP 141/88 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm and regular, weight 55 kg. Heart sounds are normal with no added murmurs, and lung bases are clear. Assessment: Stable angina. Plan: a prescription was issued for anti-anginal and protective cardiovascular therapy. He was advised to avoid heavy exertion until review, walk 20 minutes daily on flat ground, and stop smoking. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and fasting lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-02-05 09:00 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Jahid Bhuiyan, 65, male. Mr. Bhuiyan reports progressive weight gain, feeling slow and tired all day, and very dry skin. Visit note | 2025-02-05 10:00 AM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Laila Rahman, 19, female.
